options.metric: Annual motorist deaths in police-reported NYC crashes
options.reason: A fatality count directly shows the annual motorist death toll recorded in the crash data.
options.answer: Motorist deaths fell from 110 in 2013 to 81 in 2025 (about 26%), but this dataset cannot establish whether risk per mile driven declined because it contains no miles-driven measure.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how the observed annual motorist death toll changed: it was lower in 2025 than in 2013, with substantial variation between years. A count is defensible for describing total burden, but it does not measure an individual's risk or account for miles driven, so it leaves the per-mile question unanswered.

options.metric: Crashes with at least one motorist death per 100,000 reported crashes
options.denominator: All police-reported crash rows in that year
options.reason: A crash-normalized fatal-crash incidence compares the frequency of motorist-fatal crashes relative to the recorded crash volume each year.
options.answer: Motorist-fatal crashes rose from 50.1 to 87.7 per 100,000 reported crashes between 2013 and 2025, so this crash-based proxy did not decline; the data still cannot determine risk per mile driven.
options.interpretation: This framing answers how often a reported crash involved a motorist death relative to all reported crashes: the rate was higher in 2025 than in 2013 and peaked in 2023. It is a defensible crash-normalized comparison, but reported crashes are not miles driven or motorist exposure, so it cannot answer whether per-mile risk declined.
